lessons.title: Lesson 1: 🏴‍☠️ Treasure Quest (Island Math Adventure)
lessons.description: Join Mia and Leo on the pirate island map! Solve Gold Coins, Crystal Cave, Monkey's Bananas, and Balloon Bridge to reach the Golden Chest!
lessons.hint: Clue words: 'found more' and 'altogether' mean add (+); 'are gone' and 'float away' mean subtract (-)!

cards.frontHint: Look for the secret clue words in every story!
cards.explanation: Word problems tell a fun story! Look for addition words like 'more', 'altogether', and 'in all' (+). Look for subtraction words like 'left', 'are gone', and 'float away' (-). Always work step-by-step: ones, tens, then hundreds!
cards.example: Mia found clue words: 'more' means add, while 'left' means subtract.
cards.tip: Tip: Read the story, find the numbers, look for the clue word, and solve!

cards.explanation: Mia and Leo found 248 gold coins. Then they found 135 more coins. How many coins do they have altogether? 'More' and 'altogether' tell us to ADD: 248 + 135 = 383 coins! Ones: 8 + 5 = 13 (carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 4 + 3 = 8. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3.
cards.example: Mia and Leo found 248 coins and 135 more coins, making 383 gold coins altogether.
cards.tip: When ones equal 10 or more, carry 1 to the tens column!

cards.explanation: There are 376 crystals in the cave. 142 crystals are gone. How many crystals are left? 'Gone' and 'left' tell us to SUBTRACT: 376 - 142 = 234 crystals! Ones: 6 - 2 = 4. Tens: 7 - 4 = 3. Hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2.
cards.example: From 376 crystals, 142 crystals are gone, leaving 234 crystals in the cave.
cards.tip: Subtract straight down: 6 - 2 = 4, 7 - 4 = 3, 3 - 1 = 2. No regrouping needed here!

cards.explanation: The monkey has 126 bananas. Then he gets 238 more bananas. How many bananas does he have? 'Gets more' means ADD: 126 + 238 = 364 bananas! Ones: 6 + 8 = 14 (write 4, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Hundreds: 1 + 2 = 3.
cards.example: The monkey had 126 bananas, got 238 more, and now has 364 bananas.
cards.tip: Don't forget the carried 1 in the tens column: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6!

cards.explanation: There are 524 balloons on the bridge. 217 balloons float away. How many balloons are left? 'Float away' and 'left' mean SUBTRACT: 524 - 217 = 307 balloons! In ones: 4 - 7 needs regrouping! Borrow 1 ten (leaving 1 ten): 14 - 7 = 7. Tens: 1 - 1 = 0. Hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3.
cards.example: From 524 balloons on the bridge, 217 floated away, so 307 balloons are left.
cards.tip: When top ones is smaller than bottom ones, borrow 1 ten to make 14 ones!

cards.frontTitle: You Did It! Reaching the Treasure
cards.explanation: You solved all 4 stages of the island adventure: 248 + 135 = 383 coins, 376 - 142 = 234 crystals, 126 + 238 = 364 bananas, and 524 - 217 = 307 balloons! You have unlocked the Golden Treasure Chest!
cards.example: The brave math explorers unlocked the golden chest with great addition and subtraction skills.
cards.tip: Always check your work: addition can check subtraction, and subtraction can check addition!

items.explanation: 248 + 135 = 383! Mia and Leo have 383 gold coins altogether.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: 🚀 Space Odyssey (Cosmic Math Mission)
lessons.description: Blast off with Astronaut Mia & Leo! Solve Star Crystals, Moon Crater Rocks, Alien Berries, and Comet Shields to dock at Galaxy Station!
lessons.hint: Check if ones or tens need carrying or borrowing before writing your answer!

cards.frontHint: Astronauts use math to navigate the galaxy!
cards.explanation: Welcome aboard the Star Voyager rocket! Astronauts use addition and subtraction every day to measure fuel, count shiny star crystals, and calculate safe distance around comets.
cards.example: Astronauts count fuel and star crystals using 3-digit addition and subtraction.
cards.tip: Keep your numbers aligned in columns: Hundreds, Tens, and Ones!

cards.explanation: Astronaut Mia collected 314 star crystals. Then Leo found 178 more crystals. How many star crystals do they have in all? 'In all' means ADD: 314 + 178 = 492 crystals! Ones: 4 + 8 = 12 (write 2, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 1 + 7 = 9. Hundreds: 3 + 1 = 4.
cards.example: Collecting 314 crystals and 178 more gives 492 star crystals in all.
cards.tip: Regroup the ones: 4 + 8 = 12, so 2 stays in ones and 1 joins the tens!

cards.explanation: The lunar rover collected 486 moon rocks. Scientists tested 251 rocks in the spaceship lab. How many moon rocks are left? 'Left' means SUBTRACT: 486 - 251 = 235 rocks! Ones: 6 - 1 = 5. Tens: 8 - 5 = 3. Hundreds: 4 - 2 = 2.
cards.example: From 486 moon rocks, testing 251 leaves 235 rocks in the rover container.
cards.tip: Subtract each column without regrouping: 6 - 1 = 5, 8 - 5 = 3, 4 - 2 = 2!

cards.explanation: A friendly alien in a flying saucer had 237 cosmic berries. He picked 245 more berries from the glow-tree. How many berries does he have now? 'Picked more' means ADD: 237 + 245 = 482 berries! Ones: 7 + 5 = 12 (write 2, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 3 + 4 = 8. Hundreds: 2 + 2 = 4.
cards.example: The friendly alien had 237 berries, picked 245 more, and now has 482 cosmic berries.
cards.tip: Watch the tens column: 1 (carried) + 3 + 4 = 8 tens!

cards.explanation: The spaceship started with 635 shield power units. A dusty comet shower drained 318 units. How many shield units are left? 'Drained' and 'left' mean SUBTRACT: 635 - 318 = 317 units! In ones: 5 - 8 needs regrouping: borrow 1 ten to make 15 ones: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Hundreds: 6 - 3 = 3.
cards.example: From 635 shield units, losing 318 units leaves 317 shield units ready for flight.
cards.tip: 15 - 8 = 7 in ones; then the tens column becomes 2 - 1 = 1!

cards.explanation: Mission accomplished! You solved all 4 cosmic math puzzles: 314 + 178 = 492 crystals, 486 - 251 = 235 rocks, 237 + 245 = 482 berries, and 635 - 318 = 317 shield units. Welcome to Galaxy Station!
cards.example: The crew safely docked at Galaxy Station after solving all the space equations.
cards.tip: Mastering 3-digit addition and subtraction prepares you for every space mission!

lessons.title: Lesson 3: 🏰 Magic Kingdom (Dragon & Castle Carnival)
lessons.description: Step inside the royal castle carnival! Help dragon Barnaby solve Magic Potions, Ride Tickets, Fairy Cupcakes, and Castle Fireworks!
lessons.hint: Check the ones place first: do you need to carry or borrow 1 ten?

cards.frontHint: Carnival games are packed with numbers!
cards.explanation: The royal castle is celebrating with a grand carnival! Knights, friendly dragons, and wizards use math to count potion bottles, admission tickets, and sparkling fireworks.
cards.example: Dragon Barnaby counts carnival tickets and potion bottles with 3-digit math.
cards.tip: Word problems are just puzzles with a friendly story wrapped around them!

cards.explanation: The wizard brewed 265 blue bubble potions. Then he brewed 158 green sparkle potions. How many potions did he brew altogether? 'Altogether' means ADD: 265 + 158 = 423 potions! Ones: 5 + 8 = 13 (write 3, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 6 + 5 = 12 (write 2, carry 1 hundred). Hundreds: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.
cards.example: Brewing 265 blue potions and 158 green potions creates 423 potions altogether.
cards.tip: Double regrouping: ones made 13 (carry 1), then tens made 12 (carry 1)!

cards.explanation: The carousel booth had 578 ride tickets. Excited kids used 243 tickets. How many tickets are left? 'Used' and 'left' mean SUBTRACT: 578 - 243 = 335 tickets! Ones: 8 - 3 = 5. Tens: 7 - 4 = 3. Hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3.
cards.example: From 578 ride tickets, using 243 tickets leaves 335 tickets at the booth.
cards.tip: Straightforward subtraction: 8 - 3 = 5, 7 - 4 = 3, 5 - 2 = 3!

cards.explanation: The castle bakery made 184 fairy cupcakes in the morning. They baked 239 more cupcakes in the afternoon. How many cupcakes in all? 'In all' means ADD: 184 + 239 = 423 cupcakes! Ones: 4 + 9 = 13 (write 3, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 8 + 3 = 12 (write 2, carry 1 hundred). Hundreds: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
cards.example: Baking 184 cupcakes and 239 more gives 423 rainbow cupcakes in all.
cards.tip: Notice how 184 + 239 also equals 423 cupcakes: math patterns are magical!

cards.explanation: The royal guards had 642 celebration fireworks. 219 fireworks shot into the starry sky. How many fireworks remain? 'Remain' means SUBTRACT: 642 - 219 = 423 fireworks! In ones: 2 - 9 needs regrouping: borrow 1 ten to make 12 ones: 12 - 9 = 3. Tens: 3 - 1 = 2. Hundreds: 6 - 2 = 4.
cards.example: From 642 fireworks, firing 219 leaves 423 fireworks ready for tomorrow.
cards.tip: Regroup the ones: 12 - 9 = 3. Tens became 3, so 3 - 1 = 2!

cards.explanation: Hooray! You helped dragon Barnaby solve all 4 carnival challenges: 265 + 158 = 423 potions, 578 - 243 = 335 tickets, 184 + 239 = 423 cupcakes, and 642 - 219 = 423 fireworks! The King awards you the Royal Math Medal!
cards.example: The kingdom cheered for the Royal Math Champion after solving all the carnival puzzles.
cards.tip: You are now a true master of 3-digit addition and subtraction!

lessons.title: Lesson 4: 🦁 Safari Rescue (Wild Animal Park)
lessons.description: Ride the safari jeep with Ranger Mia! Solve Watering Hole Zebras, Sea Turtle Nests, Elephant Apples, and Flying Flamingos!
lessons.hint: Check the clue word: 'more' and 'altogether' (+), 'reach the ocean' or 'fly away' (-).

cards.frontHint: Park rangers use math to care for wild animals!
cards.explanation: Hop into the safari jeep! Rangers count zebras at the waterhole, check on newborn sea turtles, and pack crisp apples for hungry elephants. Math keeps all the animals safe!
cards.example: Rangers count wild animals and supply baskets with 3-digit addition and subtraction.
cards.tip: Careful observation and accurate math make a champion wildlife ranger!

cards.explanation: Rangers saw 248 zebras drinking at the waterhole. Then 165 more zebras galloped over. How many zebras are at the waterhole altogether? 'More' means ADD: 248 + 165 = 413 zebras! Ones: 8 + 5 = 13 (write 3, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 4 + 6 = 11 (write 1, carry 1 hundred). Hundreds: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.
cards.example: There were 248 zebras, then 165 more arrived, making 413 zebras altogether.
cards.tip: Carry 1 to tens (8 + 5 = 13), then carry 1 to hundreds (1 + 4 + 6 = 11)!

cards.explanation: There were 467 baby turtles resting on the beach sand. 235 turtles scrambled into the ocean waves. How many turtles are still on the beach? 'Still on the beach' means SUBTRACT: 467 - 235 = 232 turtles! Ones: 7 - 5 = 2. Tens: 6 - 3 = 3. Hundreds: 4 - 2 = 2.
cards.example: From 467 baby turtles, 235 swam away, leaving 232 turtles resting on the warm sand.
cards.tip: Clean subtraction without regrouping: 7 - 5 = 2, 6 - 3 = 3, 4 - 2 = 2!

cards.explanation: The big elephant ate 158 sweet apples for breakfast. Keepers gave him 267 more apples for lunch. How many apples did he eat in all? 'In all' means ADD: 158 + 267 = 425 apples! Ones: 8 + 7 = 15 (write 5, carry 1 ten). Tens: 1 + 5 + 6 = 12 (write 2, carry 1 hundred). Hundreds: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
cards.example: The hungry elephant ate 158 apples and then 267 more, eating 425 apples in all.
cards.tip: Regroup twice: 8 + 7 = 15 (carry 1 ten), then 1 + 5 + 6 = 12 (carry 1 hundred)!

cards.explanation: There were 625 pink flamingos wading in the lake. 218 flamingos flew into the evening sky. How many flamingos are left in the lake? 'Left' means SUBTRACT: 625 - 218 = 407 flamingos! In ones: 5 - 8 needs regrouping: borrow 1 ten to make 15 ones: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 1 - 1 = 0. Hundreds: 6 - 2 = 4.
cards.example: From 625 flamingos, 218 flew away, so 407 flamingos are left in the lake.
cards.tip: Notice the 0 in the tens place: 1 - 1 = 0 tens, giving 407!

cards.explanation: Incredible tracking! You solved all 4 wildlife challenges: 248 + 165 = 413 zebras, 467 - 235 = 232 turtles, 158 + 267 = 425 apples, and 625 - 218 = 407 flamingos. You are officially an Honorary Head Wildlife Ranger!
cards.example: The safari team honored the top ranger for excellent math and animal care.
cards.tip: You're now ready to tackle any 3-digit word problem adventure!

questions.instruction: Solve this pirate map distance puzzle.
questions.text: The pirate map measures 860 steps from the bay to Skull Rock. Mia walked 345 steps. How many steps does she have left to walk?

questions.instruction: Solve this cosmic satellite puzzle.
questions.text: A communication satellite sent 359 signals on Monday and 264 signals on Tuesday. How many signals were sent altogether?

questions.instruction: Count carnival candy apples.
questions.text: The candy booth made 425 shiny red candy apples. Happy families bought 182 apples. How many candy apples remain?
questions.hint: Ones: 5 - 2 = 3. Tens: 2 - 8 needs borrowing! Borrow 1 hundred: 12 - 8 = 4. Hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2.

questions.instruction: Count safari trees planted for elephants.
questions.text: Rangers planted 176 shady acacia trees last month and 258 trees this month. How many trees were planted in all?

questions.instruction: Solve the final treasure chest riddle.
questions.text: The legendary golden chest holds 750 shiny jewels in all. 325 jewels are sparkling diamonds. How many jewels are colorful rubies?
